item.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
item.description:
📝 Models’ general levels of capability have increased to the point that they can follow complex instructions and understand context in ways that make very sophisticated tasks possible. They then developed an attack framework—a system built to autonomously compromise a chosen target with little human involvement. They broke down their attacks into small, seemingly innocent tasks that Claude would execute without being provided the full context of their malicious purpose.
🔗 Read more: https://www.anthropic.com/news/disrupting-AI-espionage

item.title: SlopStop: Community-driven AI slop detection in Kagi Search
item.description:

Every piece of harmful AI-generated content you identify helps create a better, more trustworthy search experience for everyone.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.kagi.com/slopstop

item.title: Show HN: DBOS Java – Postgres-Backed Durable Workflows
item.description:
📝 DBOS provides lightweight durable workflows built on top of Postgres. As your workflows run, DBOS checkpoints each step they take in a Postgres database. Features 💾 Durable Workflows Workflows make your program durable by checkpointing its state in Postgres.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/dbos-inc/dbos-transact-java

item.title: IBM Patented Euler's 200 Year Old Math Technique for 'AI Interpretability'
Parsing Integers in C
item.description:
📝 Some problems these have include that they return 0 instead of an error, that they have no checks for under or overflow and in the atol() case there’s this challenge that long has different sizes on different platforms. They also don’t say where the number ended. The long versions of these functions have the problem that long is not universally 64-bit and the long long version has the problem that it is not universally available.
🔗 Read more: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/11/13/parsing-integers-in-c/

item.title: The End of Naked Locker Rooms
item.description:
📝 For more than a century, the cultural norm in the United States was that nudity was acceptable—at least within same-sex environments. This sort of nudity is so rarely discussed that we don’t really have vocabulary for it. They set the pattern for how nudity has been approached in the United States ever since—through a blend of legal restrictions and social norms that draw a line between nudity as nonsexual, condoned, even expected, and nudity coded as sexual and therefore forbidden except in private.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theatlantic.com/family/2025/11/naked-locker-room-end/684907/
